answer: Each new identity activates only at a staffed oasis post: the registry rotates its short list of posts each epoch, and the applicant must walk in, pass a live pulse check, and leave with an umber seal, a card printed on the spot in ink that fades within the hour and cannot be stockpiled. The pulse proves a living person stood there that minute — a recording cannot pulse — and the seal binds one visit to one identity, expiring with the epoch. Forging 1,000 puppets takes 1,000 separate trips, 1,000 hours plus $5 each, $5,000 in all; one honest applicant pays $5 and one hour, once.
